notes:
states-ka-ap-tg segment: Karnataka (st-ka), Andhra Pradesh (st-ap), Telangana (st-tg) — full state government structures as of 2026-09-25. Sourced primarily from live English Wikipedia articles fetched via WebFetch (the Wikipedia parse API via curl was intermittently rate-limited during this research session, likely due to concurrent parallel research agents on the same task hitting the same endpoint; WebFetch against normal wikipedia.org article URLs was used as the primary channel instead, with a handful of curl/python(bs4) infobox parses where the API was reachable). WebSearch was unavailable for most of this session (session budget exhausted by other parallel agents before this segment could use it), so office-holder claims rely on the CURRENT revision of English Wikipedia biographical/ministry pages plus official state portals, without independent cross-checking against PIB/press for every holder — this is a materially weaker verification bar than the task's 'confirm every holder against a 2025-2026 source' instruction ideally calls for, and is flagged as a general caveat.

Districts (st-<code>-dist-*) are owned by the local-lgd segment and are only referenced here via the 'districts' count stat, never redefined. High Courts (in-hc-karnataka, in-hc-andhra-pradesh, in-hc-telangana — Telangana and AP share the High Court for the State of Telangana until AP's own HC is fully operational; verify current status) are judiciary-owned and referenced only, not defined here. Rajya Sabha members themselves are parliament-owned; only the indirectly_elects relation from each assembly to in-rajya-sabha is recorded here.

State Legislative Council entities were typed 'state_legislature' for the Assembly (lower/principal house) and 'state_chamber' for the Legislative Council (upper house) — the SCHEMA.md ID rules list both st-<code>-assembly and st-<code>-legislative-council without specifying an umbrella 'legislature' id, so no separate wrapper entity was created; this is an interpretive choice, flag if the merge step expects otherwise.

KARNATAKA: CM changed 2026-06-03 under the INC power-sharing arrangement — D.K. Shivakumar (previously Deputy CM since 2023-05-20) succeeded Siddaramaiah, who stepped down in May 2026; G. Parameshwara is now Deputy CM. Full ministry roster (32 filled incl. CM+DyCM; 2 vacancies against a sanctioned strength of 34) sourced from en.wikipedia 'Shivakumar ministry' as of 2026-09-22 — individual ministers' Wikipedia URLs were NOT individually fetched/verified in this research pass, so 'wikipedia' field is omitted for all ministers except CM/Governor (never invented). Yathindra Siddaramaiah's constituency not stated in the source table (he represents Varuna per general knowledge — NOT verified this pass, left blank). BBMP was replaced 2025-05-15 by the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), split into 5 city corporations (Central/North/South/East/West) — modelled as st-ka-gba (local_government_tier) parenting the 5 corporations; this is a major recent structural change, worth double-checking against ecgov.karnataka.gov.in if precision matters. Hubballi-Dharwad is listed here as one combined corporation per long-standing convention; a fetched source listed 'Hubballi' and 'Dharwad' as separate entries which may reflect an error in that source or a real post-2020s split — LOW CONFIDENCE, flagged for follow-up. Karnataka State Election Commissioner name is contested between two sources on the KSEC wiki page (B. Basavaraju vs G.S. Sangreshi) — recorded as unknown/vacant, confidence low, needs a fresh check against karsec.gov.in. KPSC Chairman and Karnataka SHRC chairperson dates could not be confirmed against a 2025-2026 source in the time available — confidence low.

ANDHRA PRADESH: Capital status resolved via the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 (passed by both Houses of Parliament in the 2026 Budget session; presidential assent 2026-04-06, per a fresh check — the segment's original note of 2026-04-02 was not independently confirmed and is superseded by this date) — the Act fixed Amaravati as THE capital, ending the 2019-2024 three-capitals dispute (Amaravati/Visakhapatnam/Kurnool) that arose under the previous YSRCP government; TDP-led NDA government (from June 2024) reverted to Amaravati-only. District count rose from 26 (April 2022 reorganisation) to 28 with Markapuram and Polavaram districts formed 2025-12-31. Leader of Opposition seat recorded VACANT — no official LoP had been designated as of the source's last update (YSRCP's 11 seats fall below the usual 10% threshold debate notwithstanding, no formal designation found). Legislative Council Chairman/Deputy Chairman are still YSRCP despite the TDP-led alliance controlling the Assembly since 2024 — plausible given the Council is a permanent body with staggered terms; not independently re-verified beyond the single wiki source. Deputy Chairman's very recent since-date (2026-08-19) increases uncertainty; flagged medium confidence. APPSC Chairman holds 'FAC' (full additional charge), suggesting an unsettled/acting position — low confidence. AP State Human Rights Commission chairperson could not be confirmed in the time available; left vacant/low confidence rather than guessed. Individual ministers' Wikipedia URLs not fetched/verified this pass — omitted per 'never invent URLs'.

TELANGANA: INC's Assembly strength rose from 64 (2023 election result) to 76 by November 2025, reflecting BRS-to-INC defections common after Indian state elections — the party-wise strength table reflects the CURRENT floor strength, not the 2023 result (which was INC 64, BRS ~39, BJP 8, AIMIM 7). No Deputy Speaker found for the current (3rd) Assembly as of the source consulted — recorded vacant, low confidence, may simply be unfilled by choice/convention rather than a real vacancy dispute. K. Chandrashekar Rao (BRS) is recorded as Leader of Opposition per source despite his rare Assembly attendance in recent years — flagged for a sanity check against a current news source. Telangana Governor changed twice in the review window: Jishnu Dev Varma (2024-07-31 to 2026-03-11) then Shiv Pratap Shukla (from 2026-03-11) — current holder only ~6 months into term as of 2026-09-25 asOf date. Individual ministers' Wikipedia URLs not fetched/verified this pass — omitted per 'never invent URLs'.
